library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

Amrubicin is a third-generation anthracycline given to patients with small
cell lung cancer (SCLC) as a 5-minute intravenous infusion on days 1-3 of a
3- to 4-week cycle. Its active C-13 alcohol metabolite, amrubicinol, drives
severe neutropenia, the dose-limiting toxicity. Makino et al. (2026) simplified
their earlier population PK/PD model of the same 50 patients (Makino 2019) for
use in a Bayesian forecasting application. They removed the enterohepatic delay
compartment of amrubicinol and with it the SLC28A3 genotype covariate, then
re-estimated the parameters.

* PK: amrubicin follows a three-compartment model. Its only elimination is
  first-order metabolic clearance `CLp` into a one-compartment amrubicinol model
  with clearance `CLm`. Body surface area (BSA) increases `CLp`, `CLm` and the
  amrubicinol volume `Vm` through power effects.
* PD: the Friberg semi-mechanistic myelosuppression model with four maturation
  transit compartments and a linear amrubicinol effect on proliferation. A
  feedback `(Circ0 / Circ)^gamma` acts on proliferation and a second feedback
  `(Circ0 / Circ)^gamma_m` shortens the mean maturation time (MMT) while
  neutrophils are below baseline. ECOG performance status (PS) 1 shortens MMT.

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Makino_2026_amrubicin"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s00280-026-04931-8> (open access)
* Predecessor model (error structures, covariate centring, PD variability):
  <https://doi.org/10.1111/cas.14194> (open access)

# Population

All 50 patients received amrubicin monotherapy for lung cancer at the National
Cancer Center Hospital, Tokyo. They contributed 388 plasma concentrations of
amrubicin and amrubicinol and 357 absolute neutrophil counts (ANC) from the
first cycle. Supplementary Table 1 of Makino 2026 (identical to Table 2 of
Makino 2019):

| Characteristic | Value |
|---|---|
| Age, median (range) | 63.5 (39-81) years |
| Sex, male / female | 42 / 8 |
| ECOG PS 0 / 1 | 20 / 30 |
| SCLC / other histology | 42 / 8 |
| Dose 40 / 35 mg/m^2 (days 1-3) | 46 / 4 |
| BSA, median (range) | 1.65 (1.21-1.97) m^2 |
| Body weight, median (range) | 59.2 (34.9-80.3) kg |
| Baseline ANC, median (range) | 3.7 (1.4-11.9) x 10^3/mm^3 |

The Makino 2026 Results text gives the mean BSA as 1.688 m^2, the value at
which the BSA effects are centred.

# Virtual patients and dosing

Doses are entered in umol of amrubicin. The label dose is expressed as
amrubicin hydrochloride (519.93 g/mol), so 40 mg/m^2 for a 1.688 m^2 patient is
`40 * 1.688 / 519.93 * 1000` = 129.9 umol. Concentrations come back in umol/L
and are converted to ng/mL with 483.47 g/mol (amrubicin) and 485.48 g/mol
(amrubicinol) for comparison with the published values in ug*h/L.

The model has three endpoints (`Cc`, `Cc_amroh` and `ANC`), so observation rows
are placed on the `central` state with `dvid = 1`; every endpoint is returned
as a column.

```{r helpers}
mw_hcl <- 519.93
mw_amr <- 483.47
mw_amroh <- 485.48
inf_dur <- 5 / 60

make_events <- function(pat, obs_times) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(pat)), function(i) {
    amt <- pat$dose_mgm2[i] * pat$BSA[i] / mw_hcl * 1000
    rbind(
      data.frame(
        id = pat$id[i], time = c(0, 24, 48), amt = amt, rate = amt / inf_dur,
        evid = 1L, cmt = "central", dvid = NA_integer_
      ),
      data.frame(
        id = pat$id[i], time = obs_times, amt = 0, rate = 0,
        evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L
      )
    )
  })) |>
    dplyr::left_join(pat, by = "id") |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

mod <- readModelDb("Makino_2026_amrubicin")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod, which = c("omega", "sigma"))
```

# Typical patient

## Pharmacokinetics on day 1

The typical patient (BSA 1.688 m^2) receives 40 mg/m^2 on days 1-3. The table
compares the typical day-1 concentrations with the observed medians read by
the maintainers from the prediction-corrected VPC of Makino 2026 Figure 2. A
prediction-corrected median tracks the typical prediction; the reading off a
small log-scale raster is good to roughly 20-30%.

```{r typical-pk}
pk_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 72, by = 0.05), 0.25 + inf_dur, 2 + inf_dur, 4 + inf_dur, 8 + inf_dur)))
typ_pat <- data.frame(id = 1:2, dose_mgm2 = 40, BSA = 1.688, ECOG_GE1 = c(0L, 1L))
ev_typ <- make_events(typ_pat, obs_times = c(pk_times, seq(73, 42 * 24, by = 1)))
# One solve per typical patient: a multi-subject solve with the random effects
# removed warns that there is no omega.
sim_typ <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(ev_typ, ev_typ$id), function(ev) {
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev, returnType = "data.frame", atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    dplyr::mutate(id = ev$id[1], ECOG_GE1 = ev$ECOG_GE1[1])
}))

fig2 <- data.frame(
  time_after_end = c(0.25, 2, 4, 8),
  amr_paper = c(2.0, 0.7, 0.4, 0.2),
  amroh_paper = c(0.030, 0.045, 0.045, 0.045)
)
typ_day1 <- sim_typ |>
  dplyr::filter(id == 1) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time_after_end = round(time - inf_dur, 4)) |>
  dplyr::filter(time_after_end %in% fig2$time_after_end) |>
  dplyr::select(time_after_end, Cc, Cc_amroh) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(fig2, by = "time_after_end")
typ_day1 |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Time after end of infusion (h)" = time_after_end,
    "Amrubicin, model (umol/L)" = Cc,
    "Amrubicin, Figure 2 (umol/L)" = amr_paper,
    "Amrubicinol, model (umol/L)" = Cc_amroh,
    "Amrubicinol, Figure 2 (umol/L)" = amroh_paper
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Typical day-1 concentrations after 40 mg/m^2 versus observed medians read from Makino 2026 Figure 2.")

stopifnot(
  # A wrong volume, molar conversion or clearance moves these by a factor of 2 or more.
  all(abs(log(typ_day1$Cc / typ_day1$amr_paper)) < log(2)),
  all(abs(log(typ_day1$Cc_amroh / typ_day1$amroh_paper)) < log(2))
)
```

```{r typical-pk-plot, fig.cap = "Typical amrubicin and amrubicinol concentrations after 40 mg/m^2 on days 1-3 (BSA 1.688 m^2)."}
sim_typ |>
  dplyr::filter(id == 1, time <= 72) |>
  dplyr::select(time, Amrubicin = Cc, Amrubicinol = Cc_amroh) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  dplyr::filter(conc > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, conc, colour = analyte)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Concentration (umol/L)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

## Mass balance of amrubicinol

Every amrubicin molecule leaves the central compartment through `CLp` and
becomes amrubicinol, so the total amrubicinol exposure after the three doses is
`AUC(0-inf) = total dose / CLm`, independent of `CLp` and the amrubicin
distribution. A long solve has to reproduce it.

```{r mass-balance}
mb_pat <- data.frame(id = 1L, dose_mgm2 = 40, BSA = 1.688, ECOG_GE1 = 0L)
ev_mb <- make_events(mb_pat, obs_times = c(seq(0, 72, by = 0.05), seq(72.5, 400, by = 0.5)))
sim_mb <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_mb, returnType = "data.frame", atol = 1e-12, rtol = 1e-12) |>
  as.data.frame()
auc_mb <- sum(diff(sim_mb$time) * (head(sim_mb$Cc_amroh, -1) + tail(sim_mb$Cc_amroh, -1)) / 2)
dose_total <- 3 * 40 * 1.688 / mw_hcl * 1000
auc_cf <- dose_total / 140.3
c(simulated = auc_mb, closed_form = auc_cf, ratio = auc_mb / auc_cf)
# Trapezoid error on this grid is well below 0.1%; a broken formation link or
# clearance changes the ratio by tens of percent.
stopifnot(abs(auc_mb / auc_cf - 1) < 0.002)
```

## Neutrophils

```{r typical-anc-plot, fig.cap = "Typical ANC after 40 mg/m^2 on days 1-3 for ECOG PS 0 and PS 1. Dashed line: grade 4 threshold (0.5 x 10^3/mm^3)."}
sim_typ |>
  dplyr::mutate(PS = paste("ECOG PS", ECOG_GE1)) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, ANC, colour = PS)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "ANC (x 10^3/mm^3)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r typical-anc}
typ_anc <- sim_typ |>
  dplyr::group_by(ECOG_GE1) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    baseline = ANC[time == 0], nadir = min(ANC), day_nadir = time[which.min(ANC)] / 24,
    .groups = "drop"
  )
knitr::kable(typ_anc, digits = 2, caption = "Typical ANC baseline, nadir and day of nadir.")
# Before dosing the chain sits at its baseline; the shorter MMT at PS 1 brings
# the nadir earlier and deeper.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(typ_anc$baseline - 3.7) < 1e-6),
  typ_anc$day_nadir[typ_anc$ECOG_GE1 == 1] < typ_anc$day_nadir[typ_anc$ECOG_GE1 == 0]
)
```

# Simulated cohort

The cohort mirrors the study: 200 patients at 40 mg/m^2 and, as a second arm,
50 at 35 mg/m^2. BSA is drawn from a normal distribution with the reported mean
of 1.688 m^2 and an SD of 0.19 m^2 (a quarter of the 1.21-1.97 m^2 range),
truncated to that range. 60% have ECOG PS 1. All random effects come from the
model. The residual errors are held at zero (their magnitudes are not
published), so the simulated values are individual predictions.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20260728)
n40 <- 200
n35 <- 50
draw_bsa <- function(n) {
  x <- rnorm(n * 3, 1.688, 0.19)
  x <- x[x >= 1.21 & x <= 1.97]
  x[seq_len(n)]
}
cohort <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(n40 + n35),
  dose_mgm2 = rep(c(40, 35), c(n40, n35)),
  BSA = draw_bsa(n40 + n35),
  ECOG_GE1 = rbinom(n40 + n35, 1, 0.6)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = paste(dose_mgm2, "mg/m2 days 1-3"))
obs_cohort <- c(seq(0, 72, by = 0.25), seq(78, 42 * 24, by = 6))
ev_cohort <- make_events(cohort, obs_times = obs_cohort)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20260728)
sim_cohort <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_cohort, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::left_join(cohort[, c("id", "treatment")], by = "id")
```

## NCA (PKNCA)

Day-1 amrubicin exposure over 0-24 h and amrubicinol exposure over the 72 h of
the three-dose course, in ng/mL.

```{r pknca}
conc_nca <- sim_cohort |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  # Keep the 72-h course; the time-0 pre-dose record stays in.
  dplyr::filter(time %in% obs_cohort[obs_cohort <= 72]) |>
  dplyr::mutate(amr = Cc * mw_amr, amroh = Cc_amroh * mw_amroh) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, time, amr, amroh)
dose_nca <- ev_cohort |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::mutate(amt_mg = amt * mw_hcl / 1000) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, time, amt_mg)

nca_one <- function(conc_col, intervals) {
  conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(
    conc_nca, stats::as.formula(paste(conc_col, "~ time | treatment + id")),
    concu = "ng/mL", timeu = "h"
  )
  dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_nca, amt_mg ~ time | treatment + id, doseu = "mg")
  PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
}
nca_amr <- nca_one("amr", data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE))
nca_amroh <- nca_one("amroh", data.frame(start = 0, end = 72, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE))

summarise_nca <- function(res, analyte) {
  as.data.frame(res$result) |>
    dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "auclast")) |>
    dplyr::group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
    dplyr::summarise(median = median(PPORRES), p05 = quantile(PPORRES, 0.05), p95 = quantile(PPORRES, 0.95), .groups = "drop") |>
    dplyr::mutate(analyte = analyte)
}
dplyr::bind_rows(summarise_nca(nca_amr, "Amrubicin (0-24 h)"), summarise_nca(nca_amroh, "Amrubicinol (0-72 h)")) |>
  dplyr::select(analyte, treatment, PPTESTCD, median, p05, p95) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Analyte" = analyte, "Arm" = treatment, "Parameter" = PPTESTCD,
    "Median" = median, "5th percentile" = p05, "95th percentile" = p95
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Simulated NCA (Cmax in ng/mL, Tmax in h, AUC in ng*h/mL).")
```

## Comparison with the published amrubicinol exposure

Neither paper tabulates NCA. Makino 2019 (Results, Section 3.4) reports the
mean amrubicinol AUC(0-72) as 1385.9 ug*h/L in the 29 patients with grade 4
neutropenia and 1208.5 ug*h/L in the other 21, a cohort mean of 1311 ug*h/L
(92% of patients at 40 mg/m^2). Makino 2026 reports that removing the
enterohepatic delay did not meaningfully change amrubicinol AUC(0-72).

```{r nca-compare}
ref_auc <- data.frame(treatment = "40 mg/m2 days 1-3", auclast = (29 * 1385.9 + 21 * 1208.5) / 50)
sim_auc40 <- as.data.frame(nca_amroh$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(treatment == "40 mg/m2 days 1-3", PPTESTCD == "auclast")
cmp <- ncaComparisonTable(
  sim_auc40, ref_auc,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(auclast = "ng*h/mL")
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Amrubicinol AUC(0-72) at 40 mg/m^2: simulated cohort versus the Makino 2019 cohort mean.")
stopifnot(
  # Centre: a wrong molar conversion, CLm or BSA centring moves this by > 15%.
  abs(median(sim_auc40$PPORRES) / ref_auc$auclast - 1) < 0.15
)
```

## Neutropenia

In Makino 2019, 29 of 50 patients (58%) had grade 4 neutropenia (ANC below
0.5 x 10^3/mm^3) in the first cycle. Makino 2026 Figure 2 shows the observed
median ANC reaching its nadir, roughly 0.7 x 10^3/mm^3, around days 12-15.

```{r neutropenia}
anc_sum <- sim_cohort |>
  dplyr::group_by(id, treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(nadir = min(ANC), day_nadir = time[which.min(ANC)] / 24, .groups = "drop")
g4 <- anc_sum |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n = dplyr::n(),
    grade4_pct = 100 * mean(nadir < 0.5),
    median_nadir = median(nadir),
    median_day_nadir = median(day_nadir),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
g4 |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Arm" = treatment, "N" = n, "Grade 4 neutropenia (%)" = grade4_pct,
    "Median nadir (x 10^3/mm^3)" = median_nadir, "Median day of nadir" = median_day_nadir
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Simulated first-cycle neutropenia.")
g4_40 <- g4[g4$treatment == "40 mg/m2 days 1-3", ]
stopifnot(
  # 58% grade 4 in the study; the binomial SD at n = 200 is about 3.5 points and
  # the PD variability is carried from the predecessor fit, so the band is wide.
  abs(g4_40$grade4_pct - 58) < 20,
  g4_40$median_day_nadir > 10, g4_40$median_day_nadir < 17
)
```

```{r vpc-plot, fig.height = 7, fig.cap = "Simulated cohort at 40 mg/m^2 (individual predictions): median and 5th-95th percentiles, day 1 PK and first-cycle ANC. Compare Makino 2026 Figure 2."}
vpc <- sim_cohort |>
  dplyr::filter(treatment == "40 mg/m2 days 1-3") |>
  dplyr::select(time, Amrubicin = Cc, Amrubicinol = Cc_amroh, ANC) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "output", values_to = "value") |>
  dplyr::filter((output != "ANC" & time > 0 & time <= 24) | output == "ANC") |>
  dplyr::mutate(x = ifelse(output == "ANC", time / 24, time)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(output, x) |>
  dplyr::summarise(p05 = quantile(value, 0.05), p50 = median(value), p95 = quantile(value, 0.95), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(vpc, aes(x)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50)) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~output, scales = "free", ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = "Time (h for PK, days for ANC)", y = "umol/L (PK) or x 10^3/mm^3 (ANC)") +
  theme_bw()
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Molar units and the dose salt.** Both analytes were modelled in molar
  concentrations (Makino 2019 Section 2.5; Makino 2026 Figure 2 in nmol/mL, the
  same as umol/L). `Slope` therefore multiplies the amrubicinol concentration
  in umol/L. The papers do not state the molecular weight used to convert the
  dose; the vignette treats the label dose as amrubicin hydrochloride
  (519.93 g/mol), the form in which the Japanese label expresses it. Using the
  free base (483.47 g/mol) instead would raise every exposure by 7.5%.
* **BSA centring.** Makino 2019 centres continuous covariates at the cohort
  mean; the mean BSA, 1.688 m^2, is the Makino 2026 Results value. The SD it
  prints (0.522 m^2) cannot be reconciled with the 1.21-1.97 m^2 range, so the
  virtual cohort uses 0.19 m^2.
* **Rounded estimates.** Makino 2026 Table 1 prints the covariate exponents,
  `gamma`, `gamma_m` and the PS effect to one decimal place; they are used as
  printed.
* **Second feedback.** Figure 1 shows the feedback `(Circ0 / Circ)^gamma_m`
  acting on MMT, after Quartino et al. (2014). It is applied to the transit
  rate out of the progenitor pool and through the four maturation
  compartments; the proliferation rate `Kprol` and the circulating-cell loss
  rate `Kcirc` keep the baseline `Ktr` (Figure 1: `Kprol (= Ktr)`,
  `Kcirc (= Ktr)`). The papers do not write out the differential equations.
* **PD variability carried from Makino 2019.** Makino 2026 Table 1C lists only
  the PK variances, although its MMT equation carries `eta_MMT`, and the paper
  states that the PD structure is unchanged. The PD variances (Circ0 14.7%,
  MMT 31.4%, Slope 52.4% CV) are the Makino 2019 final-model values from the
  same 50 patients, converted with the same `sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1)` formula.
* **No PK covariances.** Makino 2019 estimated covariances between CLp, V3 and
  CL3; Makino 2026 reports none, so the 2026 variances are entered as a
  diagonal matrix.
* **Residual errors.** The error models (proportional for both analytes;
  additive on the Box-Cox scale with factor 0.2 for ANC) come from Makino 2019
  Section 2.5. Neither paper reports their magnitudes, so they are fixed at
  zero; simulations give individual predictions. Users who need simulated
  observations must supply residual magnitudes of their own.
* **PS coding.** The cohort had only PS 0 and PS 1, so PS enters as the 0/1
  indicator `ECOG_GE1`. The forecasting application accepts PS up to 4, but the
  model was not fitted to PS >= 2.
* **Demographics.** The Makino 2026 Results text states 80% male and 65% PS 0,
  while its Supplementary Table 1 (and Makino 2019 Table 2) give 84% male and
  40% PS 0. The table values are used.
* **Linear drug effect.** `1 - Slope * C_AMROH` is used as published. It is
  negative while amrubicinol exceeds 1 / 45.9 = 0.022 umol/L, which the typical
  patient does for most of days 1-3, so the progenitor pool shrinks during
  exposure, as in the original Phoenix model.
* **Published comparisons.** The Figure 2 values are medians read by the
  maintainers from a small raster image. The AUC reference comes from the
  Makino 2019 individual predictions, which included the enterohepatic delay.
* **Literature check.** No erratum or correction was found for either paper on
  Europe PMC (checked 2026-11-15).
